summary: spectral-core 3.0.5 exfiltrates /var/run/secrets to webhook.site at npm install via binding.gyp action
details: The package ships a binding.gyp with gypfile:true but no C/C++ source files. The sole GYP target is type:none and declares an inline action running `node -e` that reads host files including the Kubernetes/CI service-account token mount under /var/run/secrets/, /etc/hosts, and several *_test.sh / fetch.sh paths, then POSTs the collected contents over HTTPS to webhook.site at path /d6092bdc-05c0-45da-a280-c343ea6d6156. Because gypfile:true is set, `npm install` invokes `node-gyp rebuild`, which evaluates the action and executes the inline payload. Since no native sources are shipped, the manifest's only purpose is to run the exfiltration one-liner at install time. The package name resembles the legitimate @stoplight/spectral-core, consistent with a typosquat lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
